content.title: Language of change and comparison: Task 1 prepositions and forms
content.instructions: Complete each Task 1 sentence. If there is no word in brackets, write ONE preposition or function word. If there is a word in brackets, write the correct form of it (you may need to add another word such as 'the' or an intensifier).

items.prompt: Between 2010 and 2015, the price of a litre of petrol rose ___ £1.20 to £1.45.
items.model_answer: Between 2010 and 2015, the price of a litre of petrol rose from £1.20 to £1.45.
items.explanation: 'From … to …' gives the starting and finishing values of a change: rose from X to Y.

items.prompt: Over the decade, the unemployment rate fell ___ three percentage points, from 8% to 5%.
items.model_answer: Over the decade, the unemployment rate fell by three percentage points, from 8% to 5%.
items.explanation: 'By' expresses the size of the change (the difference), while 'to' gives the final value. 'Fell to 3%' would mean the rate ended at 3%, which is a different fact.

items.prompt: The figure for Germany peaked ___ 45% in 2008 before declining steadily.
items.model_answer: The figure for Germany peaked at 45% in 2008 before declining steadily.
items.explanation: 'Peak', 'stand', 'level off' and 'stabilise' are followed by 'at + value' because they describe a position, not a movement: peaked at, stood at, levelled off at.

items.prompt: There was a sharp rise ___ the number of cyclists after the new cycle lanes were opened.
items.model_answer: There was a sharp rise in the number of cyclists after the new cycle lanes were opened.
items.explanation: After nouns of change (a rise, an increase, a fall, a decline), use 'in' before the thing that changes: a rise in the number of cyclists.

items.prompt: Online sales experienced an increase ___ 20% in the final quarter of the year.
items.model_answer: Online sales experienced an increase of 20% in the final quarter of the year.
items.explanation: After a noun of change, use 'of' before the amount: an increase of 20%, a drop of 3 million. Compare 'an increase in sales' (the thing) and 'an increase of 20%' (the amount).

items.prompt: The chart shows a ___ (gradually) increase in the use of renewable energy over the period.
items.model_answer: The chart shows a gradual increase in the use of renewable energy over the period.
items.explanation: A noun (increase) is described by an adjective (gradual); a verb is described by an adverb (increased gradually). Alternating between the two patterns adds grammatical range to Task 1 answers.

items.prompt: After 2015, the number of new car registrations ___ (level) off at around two million a year.
items.model_answer: After 2015, the number of new car registrations levelled off at around two million a year.
items.explanation: 'Level off' is a phrasal verb meaning 'stop rising or falling'. A finished past period needs the past simple, and British spelling doubles the final 'l': levelled (US: leveled).

items.prompt: In 2020, Japan had ___ (high) proportion of people aged over 65 of all the countries shown.
items.model_answer: In 2020, Japan had the highest proportion of people aged over 65 of all the countries shown.
items.explanation: 'Of all the countries' compares one item with the whole group, so a superlative is required. Superlatives always take 'the': the highest, the largest, the most significant.

items.prompt: Twice ___ many women as men enrolled on nursing courses in 2019.
items.model_answer: Twice as many women as men enrolled on nursing courses in 2019.
items.explanation: Multiples are expressed with 'twice / three times + as many (countable) / as much (uncountable) + as'. Both parts of 'as … as' are needed.

items.prompt: Coffee consumption per person in Finland was ___ (considerable / high) than in Italy.
items.model_answer: Coffee consumption per person in Finland was considerably higher than in Italy.
items.explanation: A comparative adjective (higher than) can be modified by an adverb of degree: considerably, significantly, slightly, much, far. The adverb form (considerably), not the adjective (considerable), is required before a comparative.
